content: The measurement of symphysis-fundal height has largely replaced the clinical assessment of fetal size through abdominal palpation in many settings. This shift occurred because abdominal palpation has been reported to have poor performance in accurately assessing fetal size. The purpose of this review was to evaluate the impact of routinely using symphysis-fundal height measurements—specifically, the tape measurement of the distance from the pubic symphysis to the uterine fundus—during antenatal care on pregnancy outcomes. A comprehensive electronic search was conducted using the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group trials register as of August 2002. The review included controlled trials that compared the use of symphysis-fundal height measurements with the assessment of fetal size by abdominal palpation alone. One reviewer was responsible for assessing the quality of the trials and extracting the relevant data. Only one trial, which involved 1,639 pregnant women, met the inclusion criteria. The results of this trial did not reveal any significant differences in the measured outcomes between the two methods. The authors concluded that there is insufficient evidence to determine the effectiveness of symphysis-fundal height measurements during antenatal care.
